steps.caption: Bistro: three.js left, ThreeRT right
steps.say: Left of the line, three.js. Right of it, the same scene file, path traced.
The engine is called ThreeRT.

scenes.headline: How ThreeRT path-traces three.js-style code
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Albedo. ThreeRT runs three.js style code and traces its light on ray tracing hardware. Here is how, and what its sixty frames cost.

steps.say: Scene code never imports three. It imports a lookalike in physical units.

steps.term: Engine API: the calls a scene makes
steps.say: Every change becomes a call on a small engine interface.
In the native app, the script runs in QuickJS, and a Rust engine owns the scene and the frame.
In a browser, the same calls drive plain three.js. The game works. The traced light stays behind.

scenes.title: A live path ends in a cache

legend: Primary visibility: one sample a pixel
Direct light at the hit, by shadow ray
One bounce, then the light a voxel has learned
Every pixel, every frame; some train the voxels

steps.say: A live frame starts with one sample per pixel. The camera ray finds the floor.

steps.term: Next-event estimation: sample the light directly
steps.say: There, the kernel samples the lamp directly, with a shadow ray.

steps.term: Radiance cache: light stored per voxel
steps.say: Then the path bounces once and stops, reading the light from a cache voxel that other samples trained.
Every pixel, every frame, while one tile in eight trains the cache. Less noise, some bias.

scenes.title: Then the frame is cleaned up

steps.say: The raw trace is noisy and small.
It is blended with its reprojected history.
Up to five wavelet passes smooth what is still noisy.
An upscaler takes it to full size. On Bistro, the trace runs near half resolution.
Then Unreal's bloom and tone map.

steps.caption: 385 balls, a third of them lights
steps.say: Every glowing object is a light. Knock them over, and the light moves with them.

scenes.title: Bistro at night, GPU ms per frame
scenes.say: The repository's numbers, on an Apple M five. Live, fifteen and a half milliseconds at render scale point five five. Full resolution, forty.

steps.caption: reference vs ThreeRT live: delta E 3.4
steps.say: Against its own offline reference, the live frame is close, far closer than three.js.
Three.js wins on cost. Small scenes take it about a millisecond.
Tokyo, from Japan's open city model. Seventeen million triangles near the tower.
Afternoon into night, no rebuild, again through the upscaler.
On a Steam Deck, the game's own counter reads thirty-four frames a second.
Windows is an unsigned preview, and the clients are closed. The engine is MIT.
